evidence.visual_distinctiveness: contact-sheet.png — Signal system applied coherently: navy/cream dual surface alternating, single antique-gold accent confined to rules, italic emphasis and numerals, 80px grid texture on dark slides, hairline separation with no shadows or rounded corners. Reads as authored, not generated. Base 4: the design is inherited wholesale from bold-template-pack/signal rather than authored for this brief, and the visual idea is applied uniformly rather than developing across the deck. CORRECTED: one automatic deduction does apply. A decorative gold rule sits under the section label on every interior slide — under 'SEGMENT DETAIL' (slide-03.png), 'EIGHT QUARTERS, $M' (slide-04.png), 'GROSS MARGIN BRIDGE' (slide-05.png) and so on — carrying no information. That is the first automatic deduction listed for this dimension, and it is the same decorative accent line frontend-slides' own documentation bans by name. Base 4 - 1 = 3.
evidence.typographic_craft: slide-10.png, slide-04.png — deliberate three-face ladder (Source Serif 4 voice / DM Sans substance / IBM Plex Mono metadata), tabular figures in both tables, mono chrome tracked at 0.14em, consistent scale throughout. Not a 5: body sits at 21px which is the low end for a room; slide-04.png orphans 'FY25' alone on the second line of the action title; the chart's value labels sit in an aligned row rather than tracking each bar top, so they read as a number strip rather than as annotations.
evidence.hierarchy_density: slide-10.png shows ~55% empty canvas; slides 04, 07, 11 similar. The corpus explicitly specifies reading-first density and states each slide must be comprehensible without a presenter, but the delivered deck is speaker-led in feel. Hierarchy itself is strong and consistent slide to slide, which is better than the anchor-3 description, and the deck is still usable circulated, which is why this is not a 2. Action-title check passes outright: 10 of 10 content slides assert a finding rather than label a topic (100%, well above the 70% floor).
evidence.data_fidelity: fidelity.json — 56/56 figures reproduced, 0 fabricated, 0 missing. Both tables complete including total rows (slide-03.png segment table 5 rows, slide-08.png headcount table 5 rows). One sign-convention difference reviewed by hand and cleared: the deck writes 'customs declined 15.8%' in prose and '-15.8%' in the table; the corpus carries only the negative form. Same fact, correct wording. CORRECTED: the eight-quarter bar chart on slide-04 does not plot the supplied values. Measured with check_charts.py: declared heights are arithmetically perfect (36.1 -> 76.5% ... 47.2 -> 100%, a genuine zero baseline), but every bar renders at exactly 288px because those percentages resolve against a flex column of indefinite height. Values span 1.31x; rendered heights span 1.0000x. The anchor for 5 requires that charts plot the actual supplied values, and this one encodes nothing while its own footer states 'Bars plotted from a zero baseline'. Anchor 3 — all figures correct, chart not verifiable against source — is the fit. See charts.json.
evidence.content_fidelity: contact-sheet.png — all ten corpus sections represented (headline, segment detail, eight-quarter trend, margin bridge, concentration, last-mile, headcount, risks, asks, Q4 outlook). Nothing invented. Emphasis is preserved: the margin compression is carried in the headline alongside the revenue growth rather than buried. Noted but not penalised per rubric: the deck does not carry forward the corpus's top-level 'all content is fictional' marker.
evidence.deliverable_integrity: deck.html lines 10-13 load three font families from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com — 3 remote runtime dependencies. Offline, or if the CDN moves, typography falls back to Georgia and system stacks, which is precisely what the skill's own anti-slop rules forbid. This maps exactly to anchor 3: 'works but has external dependencies that will break offline or when the CDN moves.' Everything else is clean: one 36 KB file, no external scripts, opens with no server, keyboard and click navigation work, fixed stage scales and letterboxes correctly, print CSS emits one 1920x1080 page per slide.
evidence.effort_to_acceptable: One correction turn. First output collided text on slide 10: '.list li' was 'display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2em 1fr', which promoted every inline <em> to its own grid item, wrapping '$2.4M' on top of 'capex' and '60%' on top of 'of projected volume'. Fixed by switching the bullet marker to absolute positioning. Answering the skill's four Phase-1 interview questions is not counted as a correction turn per the protocol — those answers came from the corpus brief.

findings.summary: The skill's Core Principle #1 is 'Zero Dependencies - single HTML files with inline CSS/JS', but its own html-template.md line 16 prescribes a remote font stylesheet link, and signal/design.md documents a Google Fonts preconnect pattern. Every deck produced this way carries a network dependency for its typography. The two instructions conflict, and the conflict is inherited by the output.

bold-template-pack/selection-index.json labels the Signal template density 'high', while templates/signal/design.md states 'Density philosophy: medium-low and asymmetric' and 'Don't fill more than half a typical slide with content'. Selecting Signal for an explicitly reading-first brief on the strength of the index metadata, then generating from design.md, yields a sparse speaker-led deck for a dense reading-first request. The selection metadata and the design recipe disagree.

An em-dash bullet implemented as a two-column CSS grid on the <li> promotes every inline <em> to a grid item, producing overlapping text. Caught only in a rendered screenshot; the source reads as correct. Concrete instance of why principle 07 (render it and look at it) is load-bearing.

The eight-quarter trend spans 36.1 to 47.2 on a zero baseline, so all eight bars look nearly identical and the chart communicates little beyond the printed values. Honest but weak as a visualization. A truncated axis would read better but would need an explicit break marker to stay honest.

notes: FIRST RUN — treat as harness validation more than as a verdict. Three caveats, all material: (1) the operator who executed the skill also wrote the rubric and the corpus, and also scored the result, so this is not an independent measurement; operator_conflict is set for that reason. (2) The run was not blind — there was only one entry, so anonymize.py could not do anything useful. (3) n=1 against known generative variance; a second run of the same pairing could land several points away. The single most valuable contribution anyone can make to this repo is an independent re-score of this exact pairing from the committed artifacts. This run did surface two real defects in the harness itself, both now fixed: check_fidelity.py was counting figures from the corpus operator brief (which no deck should reproduce) and was reporting sign-convention differences as fabrication.
